findings.title: Transitional compute SA secret binding has no removal enforcement — will silently undermine SA segregation
findings.explanation: This binding was re-added to bridge the Cloud Run SA migration and is explicitly documented as temporary. However, a comment is the only guard — there is no Terraform mechanism (variable gate, lifecycle rule, or expiry condition) to enforce removal. The entire purpose of HOLDEN_AI_005 (creating a dedicated fuel-backend SA) was to eliminate the compute SA's access to secrets; leaving this binding in place permanently defeats that fix. Comments rot; code doesn't.
findings.remediation: Add a boolean variable `var.compute_sa_secret_access_enabled` defaulting to `false` with `count = var.compute_sa_secret_access_enabled ? 1 : 0` on the resource. Set it to `true` in tfvars only during the migration window, forcing an explicit decision to keep or remove it on every apply. Alternatively, remove it now — the fuel-backend SA is deployed and serving traffic.

findings.title: `time_sleep` of 90s has no buffer above GCP's documented 120s maximum IAM propagation window
findings.explanation: GCP documents IAM propagation as typically completing within 60 seconds but potentially taking up to 7 minutes in rare edge cases. The 90-second sleep is 30 seconds above the typical case but provides no buffer above the documented maximum. A deployment during a period of elevated GCP IAM latency will still fail, requiring a manual re-run. This is the same failure mode that prompted adding the sleep in the first place.
findings.remediation: Increase `create_duration` to `"120s"` to cover the stated typical maximum, and document in the comment that occasional failures may still require a re-run for edge cases. Alternatively, use `"300s"` (5 minutes) as a conservative buffer — the tofu job already has a 30-minute timeout so this is acceptable.

findings.title: KMS crypto keys have no description or labels — indistinguishable in GCP audit logs and console
findings.explanation: Both KMS keys (`garmin-tokens` and `sqlite-data`) have no `description` field and no labels. In GCP audit logs, KMS operations show the key resource name but not its purpose. With two keys in the same project encrypting different classes of data (session tokens vs. health/food data), distinguishing them in a security investigation or compliance audit requires reading the Terraform source. Labels and descriptions are the standard mechanism for this.
findings.remediation:
Add `description` and `labels` to both keys:
```hcl
description = "Encrypts Garmin OAuth session tokens stored in SQLite"
labels = { purpose = "garmin-token-encryption", environment = "production" }
```

suggested_policies.rationale: google_kms_crypto_key resources without a description field are common and create operational confusion in multi-key projects. A description is an unambiguous attribute check with no false positives. coverage_by_type for google_kms_crypto_key currently only includes key-rotation checks — no description/label coverage exists.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_003
name: KMS crypto keys must have a description
principle: governance
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  KMS keys without descriptions are indistinguishable in audit logs, billing
  reports, and the GCP console. When multiple keys exist in a project, operators
  must cross-reference Terraform source to determine which key encrypts which
  data class. A description field provides inline context at the point of use.
remediation: |
  Add a description = "..." field to the google_kms_crypto_key resource
  explaining what data this key protects and in which environment.
resources:
  google_kms_crypto_key:
    not_null:
      - description
